title: Hypformer: Exploring Efficient Transformer Fully in Hyperbolic Space

problem.claim: Transformers have not been fully adapted to hyperbolic space for modeling complex structured data, and existing hyperbolic self-attention has quadratic time complexity with respect to input-token count.

gap.claim: Prior work mainly modified self-attention and lacked well-defined hyperbolic counterparts for essential Transformer modules, including linear layers, LayerNorm, activations, and dropout.

contributions.claim: The authors propose Hypformer, a hyperbolic Transformer based on the Lorentz model of hyperbolic geometry.
Hypformer introduces two foundational blocks defining essential Transformer modules in hyperbolic space.
Hypformer develops a linear self-attention mechanism in hyperbolic space.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe Hypformer as a novel hyperbolic Transformer and state that its linear self-attention enables processing billion-scale graph data and long-sequence inputs in hyperbolic space for the first time.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments across various datasets confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of Hypformer.
The authors report that Hypformer has potential as an effective and scalable solution for large-scale data representation and large models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hyperbolic geometry is presented as promising for complex structured data with tree-like or hierarchical structure.
Research adapting Transformers to hyperbolic space remains limited, with prior attempts focused mainly on self-attention and not producing a complete hyperbolic Transformer.
The stated obstacles are missing hyperbolic Transformer modules and quadratic complexity in existing hyperbolic self-attention.
Hypformer addresses these obstacles with foundational hyperbolic Transformer blocks and linear self-attention based on the Lorentz model.
Experiments across various datasets are reported to support the method's effectiveness and efficiency.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical experimental results.
The abstract does not describe the architecture of the two foundational blocks.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or complexity bounds for the linear self-attention mechanism.
The abstract does not independently verify the claimed first-time capability or billion-scale and long-sequence processing.
